s1.syndrome_frame: A subcutaneous mass with recent growth and tenderness on the lower leg
salient_findings: Painful nodule on the lower part of the right leg
Enlargement and tenderness of the lesion over the past 6 months
Irregular, firm, erythematous, mobile, tender mass
key_facts: 40-year-old man
Lesion stable in size and painless for 4 years
No history of trauma
No personal or family history of malignancy
Mass measuring 3.5 × 2.3 × 1.7 cm
No popliteal or inguinal lymphadenopathy
Normal routine blood tests
Negative tests for hepatitis B surface antigen and HIV
Lobulated, tan-gray, firm mass on gross examination
Dermal tumor extending into the superficial subcutis
Nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells on light microscopy
Mitotic figures, including atypical forms, measured 7–8 per 10 high-power fields

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the description of a subcutaneous mass with recent growth and tenderness, and immunohistochemical staining showed strong positivity for vimentin

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the presence of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells and high mitotic activity

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic hyalinizing angiectatic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the presence of a lobulated, tan-gray, firm mass and nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells

shortlist.label: Atypical fibroxanthoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the presence of a dermal tumor extending into the superficial subcutis and high mitotic activity

shortlist.label: Sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the presence of a subcutaneous mass with recent growth and tenderness, and immunohistochemical staining showed focal positivity for Melan-A and HMB-45

raw.rationale: The presence of nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei, and prominent nucleoli, along with a high mitotic rate and atypical forms, is consistent with atypical fibroxanthoma. The tumor's location on the lower leg, a common site for this tumor, and the absence of significant lymphadenopathy or systemic symptoms also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: Typically shows a more uniform storiform or cartwheel pattern and often expresses CD34, which was not mentioned in the immunohistochemical results

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: Would typically show more pronounced smooth muscle differentiation and express markers such as desmin or smooth muscle actin, which were not mentioned

rejected.label: Pleomorphic hyalinizing angiectatic tumor
rejected.why: Characterized by a distinctive hyalinizing vascular pattern and often expresses CD31 or factor VIII, which were negative in this case

rejected.label: Sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma
rejected.why: Typically shows a more sclerotic stroma and often expresses MUC4, which was not mentioned in the immunohistochemical results
